### 2026-10-08 – Today I continued cleaning up the schematic from yesterday. At first I thought I would just spend my time manually rerouting wires around the board to make it look neater. Instead, I learned how to us

**2h**

Today I continued cleaning up the schematic from yesterday. At first I thought I would just spend my time manually rerouting wires around the board to make it look neater. Instead, I learned how to use net labels to clean up the design. This makes the schematic look significantly more organized and much easier to read than having messy wires crossing each other all over the place!

**1h**

I started moving my finished schematic into the PCB layout! While I was doing this, I found a lot of errors because several of my parts didn't have the correct footprints assigned to them. I had to check every part, figure out the errors, and assign the right footprints so everything would fit properly on the board.

### 2026-10-09 – I finished routing the pcb wiring. It took me so much time to get the custom boundary right because the first time it was too big, the second time it was too small, and the third time it was just righ

**3h**

I finished routing the pcb wiring. It took me so much time to get the custom boundary right because the first time it was too big, the second time it was too small, and the third time it was just right. Next I encountered a problem: I didn't assign the footprints correctly, so it took me time to fix it. Then the routing of wires took me time because I was trying to understand how to do it and I kept not having enough space, so I tweaked some copper zoning and now I have completed it.
